El dispositivo (diodo o transistor) y su: The device (diode or transistor) and its external circuit each impose a relationship between voltage and current. The circuit's comes from Kirchhoff's law for the loop and is a straight line, the load line. The device's is its characteristic curve. Both hold at the same time at a single point, the operating (or quiescent) point $Q$.
Con una fuente $V_S$ y una resistencia $: With a source $V_S$ and a resistor $R$ in series, the line is $I_D = (V_S − V_D)/R$ and the curve follows the Shockley equation, $I_D = I_S (e^(V_D/(n V_T)) − 1)$, with $V_T = kT/q ≈ 25.85 "mV"$ at 300 K. Since the equation has no algebraic solution, it is solved numerically; on paper the ideal model ($V_D = 0$) or the constant-voltage model ($V_D ≈ 0.7 "V"$ for silicon) is used.
En polarización fija o por divisor de te: With fixed bias or voltage-divider bias, the base current is computed with the Thévenin equivalent of the base circuit, $I_B = (V_"BB" − V_"BE")/(R_"BB" + (β + 1) R_E)$. In active, $I_C = β I_B$ and the load line is $V_"CC" = V_"CE" + I_C R_C + I_E R_E$. If $V_"CE" < V_"CE,sat"$ comes out, the transistor is in saturation and $I_C < β I_B$; if $V_"BB" ≤ V_"BE"$ it is in cutoff. A point near the center of the line allows amplifying without clipping the signal; near the ends, the transistor works as a switch.
La puerta no consume corriente, así que: The gate draws no current, so $V_"GG"$ comes from the voltage divider and $V_"GS" = V_"GG" − I_D R_S$. In saturation ($V_"DS" ≥ V_"GS" − V_t$) $I_D = 1/2 K (V_"GS" − V_t)^2$; in triode, $I_D = K [(V_"GS" − V_t) V_"DS" − V_"DS"^2/2]$; below $V_t$ it is in cutoff. The load line is $V_"DD" = V_"DS" + I_D (R_D + R_S)$.
